subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures keep the asynchronous accepted `sessions_spawn` contract and terminalize visibly, or should Docker startup be preflighted enough to reject before returning accepted?
rationale: The choice affects the public spawn contract, gateway waits, subagent registry state, session projections, and the overlapping lifecycle PR, so automation should not choose the permanent behavior alone.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed, logged terminal startup failure visible in session history, subagents list, and agent waits.

options.title: Preflight Sandbox Before Accept
options.body: Move enough Docker startup validation before acceptance to reject immediately, accepting extra latency and upgrade/contract implications.

options.title: Resolve Through Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Use the broader lifecycle issue as the implementation path while keeping this sandbox issue as the required live repro and acceptance case.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a typed, logged terminal startup failure visible in session history, subagents list, and agent waits.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history around sessions_spawn and sandbox inheritance makes this the best available owner for the API/behavior contract choice.
